workers.summary: I found three intraday ES/NQ candidates that board.md and ledger.csv (N=173) do not cover. Ranked by how testable they are here: (1) gamma-conditioned intraday momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens, JFE 2021), now testable because six independent GitHub mirrors of the SqueezeMetrics daily GEX history agree exactly and run to 2026-10-02; (2) VWAP trend (Zarattini & Aziz 2023, working paper), which flips about 16 times a day, so ES costs come to about 25 bp/day against a median |open-to-close| of 45 bp; (3) an asymmetric reversal after large intraday down-moves (Vlasiuk & Smirnov, arXiv Nov 2025, not peer-reviewed). I ran no return backtest and spent no N. None of these is an edge, every paper host was EGRESS_BLOCKED, and no post-publication persistence evidence was found for any of them.

findings.claim: Coverage check: the board and ledger already cover TOTM, overnight-gap fade (H0012), pre-FOMC drift, FOMC even weeks, 5-min ORB, last-half-hour momentum (H0006, closed), Beat-the-Market noise-boundary momentum (H0005/H0011), TJR, trend and stack. The three candidates below are outside that list. Two of them sit next to closed families, and the director has to decide whether they count as new families.

findings.claim: Candidate 1 (most testable, peer-reviewed): gamma-conditioned market intraday momentum. Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens, 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics, Oct 2021. Sample: 60+ futures (equities, bonds, commodities, FX), 1974-2020. The rest-of-day return (previous close to the last 30 minutes) predicts the last 30 minutes, and the effect reverts over the next days. For the S&P the momentum is present when the negative-gamma-exposure proxy (NGE) is negative and gets stronger as it gets more negative. On days with positive NGE there is no significant momentum. Barbon & Buraschi ('Gamma Fragility', working paper) add that momentum comes with negative dealer gamma and reversal with positive gamma, interacting with illiquidity. No Sharpe, drawdown, cost figure or post-2020 persistence evidence was obtained.

findings.claim: Candidate 1 trades rarely and in clusters. In the SPY 1m 2019-01-02..2025-07-18 sample (1645 RTH days), the previous day's GEX was below zero on 203 days: 19/31/16/104/23/1/9 for 2019..2025. Over 2011-05-03..2026-10-02 there are 347 such days out of 3878. That is about 30 trades a year, half of them in 2022. Under the board's rule-3 definition (z = 3.44 at N=173), n = 203 needs a per-trade net Sharpe of at least 3.44/sqrt(203) = 0.24. At about 30 trades a year it cannot carry the prop goal by itself, so it is at best a regime filter or overlay.

findings.claim: Candidate 2 (most testable on price alone, weakest evidence): VWAP trend. Zarattini & Aziz, 'Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP): The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems', SSRN 4631351, Nov 2023, working paper. Rule: long when the 1m close is above the session VWAP, short when below, reverse on every cross, flat at the close. Reported on QQQ 2018-01-02..2023-09-28: $25k grew to $192,656 (+671%), Sharpe 2.1, max drawdown 9.4%, 'net of commissions'. No slippage model is mentioned, and no post-publication result was found.

It models no spread or slippage ('No bid/ask spread or slippage modelled', engine/broker.py:93) and reports live-bot losses of -$1,458 and -$600 on 2026-04-06/07 (docs/bad_day_patterns.md). This family overlaps H0005/H0011: Beat the Market, by the same authors, uses VWAP as its trailing stop.

findings.claim: Cost check on candidate 2 (no P&L computed): on 1m bars the VWAP rule makes a median 16 entries a day on SPY 2019-2025 (mean 17.7, p90 31; 16.9-18.5 every year) and a median 15 on NQ RTH 2020-08..2025-11 (mean 16.4). At the board's 0.6 ES-point round trip that costs a median 25.0 bp a day (mean 28.3 bp), against a median SPY |open-to-close| of 45.4 bp (NQ 64.9 bp). On futures the 1m-flip version therefore has to capture more than half of the typical day's whole move just to break even. Any test should fix a coarser bar (e.g. 5m or 15m) or a band before the first run.

findings.claim: Candidate 3 (testable approximately, lowest evidence): asymmetric reversal after large intraday down-moves. Vlasiuk & Smirnov (Columbia), 'Push-response anomalies in high-frequency S&P 500 price series', arXiv 2511.06177, Nov 2025, not peer-reviewed. Data: SPY NBBO event time, about 1,500 trading days. Responses near zero for lags of 1-5,000 ticks, then tails. Large negative pushes are followed by stronger positive responses than equal positive pushes. No costs, Sharpe, drawdown or trading rule were obtained. It can only be approximated on the 1m bars here, not tick data. It differs from H0012 because it fires at any time of day, not at the open.

workers.summary: I pre-registered and ran one new hypothesis, H-2026-10-05, an intraday IBS reversal on the S&P (3 variants). The rule: if the prior session closed in the bottom 20% of its range, go long; if in the top 20%, go short. Enter at the 09:31 open, stop at k x ATR14 (the average daily range of the last 14 sessions), no target, exit at the 15:59 close, 0.6 pt round trip. The rules were written to builder/prereg_ibs_intraday.txt and sha256-stamped at 2026-10-05T04:03:13Z before any code ran. It fails the decision rule I set in advance: variant A's net mean is -0.0097R (p5 -0.0871) at 74.7 trades/yr, and the 2015-18 half is net -0.0539R, so the family should be closed with no retuning. Gross is slightly positive (+0.048R for A), but costs (median 0.061R) take it all. Not an edge, and it cannot pass gate rule 1 anyway, because no ledger row existed before the run.
